request.spec:
Backing is now the sum of the patrons' settled figures over their SETTLED claims dated within the
90 days up to and including the sheet's today (each at its frozen figure), 0.00 with none.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Backing is now the sum of the patrons' settled figures over their SETTLED claims dated within the
90 days up to and including the sheet's today (each at its frozen figure), 0.00 with none.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A person's Backing now adds up only their patrons' settled claims dated in the last 90 days, counting today. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The change is all in one file, `src/main/frontend/features/patrons/patrons.slot.tsx`. The server, stored data and audit records didn't need changing, because Backing was already worked out only on the page.

- **Which claims count:** only SETTLED claims dated from today minus 89 days up to today. On a sheet whose today is 2026-03-10, that means claims from 2025-12-11 onward.
- **The amount used:** each claim's due as fixed when it was settled, so a later rate change doesn't alter it. With no matching claims, Backing shows 0.00.
- **Before:** it added up the patrons' due-totals, which included open claims and the cap.

**Settled with no rate:** if a claim was settled when its grade had no rate, nothing was fixed at settlement. For those, Backing uses the same live figure the claim's own due column shows: n/a (left out of the sum) while there's no rate, a computed figure once a rate exists. The tests don't cover this case. If such a claim should always count as nothing, that's a one-line change.

The first test run failed because the page crashed while the sheet's date was still loading and the 90-day calculation had no date to work from. I added a check for that, and the passing run includes the fix.
